newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea appoints caretaker prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea appoints caretaker prime minister.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea cabinet on Thursday appointed Mining and Petroleum Minister John Giheno as acting prime minister to replace Sir Julius Chan after Chan decided to stand down to end 10 days of political turmoil.
Giheno made the announcement himself to reporters, and added that Forests Minister Andrew Baing would be acting deputy prime minister.

Chan told parliament on Wednesday that he, Deputy Prime Minister Chris Haiveta and Defence Minister Mathias Ijape would step aside for the duration of an inquiry into a controversial $36 million contract for mercenaries.
He had come under widespread pressure to quit for hiring the mercenaries to crush an uprising on copper-rich Bougainville island.

The worst crisis in Papua New Guinea's 22 years of independence started on March 17 when army leader Jerry Singirok turned on Chan, demanding he quit and expel some 70 African mercenaries flown in by British company Sandline International.

Chan in turn sacked the popular Singirok, who retained the loyalty of his troops while holed up throughout the crisis in the main Murray barracks in the South Pacific nation's capital. The mercenaries meanwhile left Port Moresby in batches.
